## 2. Senior Robotics Engineer @ Wastefull Insights (Vadodara, India · Aug 2022 – Nov 2025)

- The 80% Compute Overhead Reduction (The Latency Crisis Case Study):
  - Initial State: Python perception loop running 4x 1080p RTSP feeds at 30 FPS. End-to-end latency was 195ms (Image capture: 5ms, GPU pre-processing: 50ms, Model inference: 80ms, Python post-processing: 60ms). GPU utilization was pinned at 95% on expensive desktop RTX GPUs.
  - Profiling & Root Cause: Profiled with NVIDIA Nsight and PyTorch profilers. Bottlenecks were memory copies between host/device and unoptimized post-processing loops.

    1. Model Optimization: TensorRT FP16/INT8 quantization + model pruning reduced inference from 80ms to 35ms.
    2. Pipeline Architecture: Replaced custom decoding with NVIDIA DeepStream SDK for hardware-accelerated zero-copy video decoding.
    3. C++ Migration: Rewrote hot-path post-processing (bounding box filtering, line crossing, tracking) in multithreaded C++ with shared memory buffers.
    4. Asynchronous Queuing: Batched 2 frames per GPU call while concurrently capturing the next frames in a double-buffered queue.
  - Quantified Result: Latency plummeted from 195ms to 42ms (<1 frame delay). GPU utilization dropped from 95% to 20%, allowing deployment on power-efficient NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier edge modules (slashing compute hardware cost by 4x).
- Multi-Stream Video Analytics:

- Motion Control Optimization (Delta & 3-Axis Gantries):
  - Re-architected trajectory generation from scratch using S-curve acceleration profiling instead of trapezoidal motion.
  - Analyzed and eliminated inertial jerk losses by 15%, reducing mechanical vibration and settling time.
  - Boosted pick-and-place cycle speed by 40% and overall cell efficiency by 80%.
- Multi-Robot Fleet Coordination & Industrial PLC:
  - Coordinated multi-arm picking cells processing 10,000+ items daily (500+ picks/hour per arm) with dynamic task allocation.

- Fleet Telemetry & Predictive Analytics:

- The Thermal Throttling Incident (Factory Floor Case Study):

# Technical Problem-Solving Methodology
When explaining how you tackle tough technical problems, follow Tejas's systematic 4-step framework:
1. Problem Definition & Empirical Profiling: Measure baseline metrics first (latency breakdown, GPU utilization, frame drops, mechanical jerk). Never optimize without profiling data.
2. Physics & Root-Cause Understanding: Model the physical constraints (memory bandwidth, thermal limits, motor torque-speed curves, friction).
3. Staged Implementation & Simulation Validation: Validate algorithmic changes in simulation or isolated test benches before deploying to production hardware.
4. Telemetry-Backed Production Verification: Verify improvements against quantified acceptance criteria (e.g. latency cut from 195ms to 42ms, pick speed up 40%) and log runtime metrics.
